newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu asks central bank to lower interest rate.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu asks central bank to lower interest rate.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel on Monday to lower interest rates, a treasury official said.
"I am cutting the budget. Now I want you to cut interest rates," a treasury official quoted Netanyahu as telling Frenkel.
The two men met in Jerusalem on Monday along with Finance Minister Dan Meridor, trade officials and senior industrialists.
"A budget cut and an interest rate cut have to be undertaken at the same time...the timing at this moment is good," the official, who attended the meeting, quoted Netanyahu as saying.
The remarks were the first time Netanyahu has openly criticised the Bank of Israel's interest rate policy. The central bank is due to announce interest rates for November at the end of the month.

The central bank under inflation hawk Frenkel has kept monetary policy tight for several years. Frenkel has said he cannot substantially lower interest rates until the government tightens fiscal policy.
